_comment: Ratchet baseline for the Datastore Isolation workflow (TD-881).
These ceilings MAY ONLY EVER FALL. CI fails when a run exceeds one, which is
the signal that something new in the suite reaches the operator's real
services. When a run comes in under, lower the number so the ground gained
cannot be given back.
WHAT IS COUNTED
The gated number is data-carrying connections PLUS connections the classifier
could not decide. Undecided ones are included deliberately: a connection that
did not declare itself inside the budget might have carried data, and scoring
it as a harmless probe would let a real regression hide behind a slow runner.
See Tripwire._classify. Bare probes -- a peer that closed having sent nothing
-- are a definite outcome and are not gated.
IT IS NOT ZERO, DELIBERATELY
Zero would require every test that spawns a real hook script to be re-pointed
at a throwaway instance -- roughly eighteen more files, tracked separately as
a burn-down. What protects the operator is the network namespace: every one of
these connections lands on the tripwire inside the namespace and reaches
nothing real. These numbers measure test hygiene; the namespace is the safety.
THESE NUMBERS ARE MEASURED IN CI, AND A LOCAL RUN WILL NOT MATCH
The two environments target different ports, because a maintainer machine has
an AI-Memory install and a runner does not:
On a runner QDRANT_GRPC_PORT is unset, so qdrant-client falls back to its own
gRPC default of 6334; locally that variable is set to 26351 by the operator's
docker/.env, which src/memory/classifier/config.py loads into the environment.
Langfuse is absent on a runner, so 23100 goes quiet there while dominating
locally. Both 26351 and 6334 therefore have to be watched -- an earlier design
watched neither.
The gate runs in CI, so these ceilings are CI-referenced. Do not raise them to
accommodate a local run; a local total above max_gated is expected.
max_gated is 40 against a measured 27, and jitter_allowance is set so that
27 does not read as a drop worth tightening. The headroom exists because the
6334 gRPC count comes from connection retries and moves run to run. If a run
comes in materially below 27, lower both.
26350 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS
It is the Qdrant REST port -- the one tests actually write through -- and it
measured exactly 4 on both a runner and a maintainer machine. max_per_port
gates it exactly, so a new test reaching the datastore fails immediately even
though the whole-suite total carries headroom for gRPC retry jitter.
Before this work the same measurement was 147 accepts / 122 data-carrying
across the three ports then being watched, with 101 on 26350. Measured on the
CI-scope suite (-m 'not regression and not quarantine') with a cleared
environment, inside a network namespace, ordering fixed via -p no:randomly.
A CEILING NEEDS A FLOOR UNDER IT
min_tests is not a ratchet -- it is what stops the ratchet grading a run that
never happened. Every ceiling here is satisfied most easily by a suite that
does not execute: it connects to nothing, so it scores zero. The CI-scope run
reports 6486 tests (5802 passed, 684 skipped), and the floor sits at 5000 so a
run that collects a fraction of the suite fails instead of setting a new best
score. Raise it when the suite grows; a floor that trails far behind the real
count stops catching partial selections. See check_run_happened.

pre_fix_reference.note: Same command before this work; 23100 and 6334 were not yet watched.
